intelligence.human_view: The ten notes are one system described from four sides, and the sides only make sense together. The showing side is a single law in three shapes: never make the citizen face the whole thing at once. A long text unfolds one paragraph at a time because a wall of text is a refusal to read — and an unread agreement is not an agreement. A slideshow ends at its last image because forcing it sideways into the letter breaks both the slideshow and the letter — two presentations, separate destinations, linked by buttons, never one flow forced sideways. The legal pages sit in a quiet row because the thing a citizen came for is the feature and the thing the system owes them is small, quiet, and always there — and the flagged items (governing law, jurisdiction, dispute resolution, data controller) stay flagged, never invented, because a legal page that invents its jurisdiction is worse than a missing one. The spreading side is the same law applied to the builders: mirror success and the clone trick are both refusals to re-invent. A tactic that works — the unfold, the three-bar stack, the clone trick — is captured and carried everywhere it fits, judged by the sense check on the receiving page; and depth, which the seats could not make, is now a two-second move any seat can do — clone once, behind, nudge a tad — proven on the hardest object in the system, a person's name. The judging side is the scorecard, and it exists because a round can pass every check and still miss: the checks measure the brief, the scorecard measures the page — ten loves named and protected, ten don't-loves filed as items in his words, ten done ten times better. The entering side is the citizen's side of the same laws: the feeds live on the day because the day is the unit of a life; the free walk ends in the Hub because a front door that only opens for paying citizens is not a front door; three ways in because no way in is second-class; and the word is THING because "space" is our word and "thing" is theirs — the dog, the farm, the craft, the cause — and a system that calls a person's passion a space has already misunderstood them. Show it one beat at a time, spread what works, judge the whole page, let them in by their own way — that is one system, not four laws.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a magic house with three front doors. Every door is beautiful. You pick the one you like. One little bit at a time, tap, tap, tap. And you find your people by your thing!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — nobody wants a great big wall of words, so you give them a little bit at a time, tap, tap, tap, and before they know it they've read the whole thing. When something works beautifully, you use it everywhere it fits — that's how a house stays tidy. And a good house has more than one way in, every one a proper welcome: come straight in and give your name, or read all about it first, or watch the lovely pictures. Everybody's got their thing, dear — and that's where they'll find their people.
intelligence.naya_view: Never a wall. One paragraph at a time, next button each time. Mirror what works everywhere it fits — and give everything depth, one clone behind, nudged a tad. Judge the whole page, ten and ten and ten. And every way in is extraordinary — agree by entering, read it, or go through the visual and come back. We got you.
